findings: Revision 1 addresses the primary attack: a mechanical fabric can manipulate institutional outcomes through scheduling and selective delivery without claiming truth authority.
Authorized mechanical envelopes and explicit policy-laundering prohibitions make the influence channel visible and testable.
conditions: Starvation, selective suppression, priority inversion, replay amplification, and missing-transport-vs-negative-evidence must be mandatory hostile tests.
Mechanical optimization policy must be attributable and auditable.
A compromised FABRIC must have a tested containment path that preserves AETHER semantic correctness.
Any future FABRIC interpretation of authority-bearing tokens requires separate review.
residual_uncertainty: Denial, selective delay, and topology bias remain substantial attack surfaces even when semantic authority is protected.
